cim_eredeti: AI for Science expands to foundations and institutions
szoveg_eredeti:
We’re highlighting 20 scientific foundations, institutions, and research groups from around the world that we’ve partnered with in an expansion of our AI for Science program, which gives free Claude credits to researchers working on high-impact scientific projects.

We started the AI for Science program in May 2025 with the belief that AI could significantly speed up scientific progress. Our goal is to increase access to AI tools and resources to enable researchers to deepen and expand their own scientific work. (Over the last few months, we’ve also launched our discounted Team plan for scientists and have supported hundreds of projects across biology, medicine, physics, chemistry, climate science, and mathematics.)

Scientists have told us that they’re working with Claude to generate hypotheses, design experiments, swiftly analyze complex data, and communicate findings. With scientists at the center of this transformation, the field is setting the questions and developing the research projects that will help us tackle some of humanity’s toughest problems.

Over the past year, we’ve started to expand this work and partner with scientific organizations to build collaborative research projects. For instance, we partnered with HHMI Janelia Research Campus to develop the Model Hardware Standard (MHS), a shared specification that lets AI agents safely operate lab instruments. MHS is currently in research preview. We also support the Allen Institute, a leader in creating large open datasets and tools to advance research on the brain, cells, and the immune system. The institute is building teams of AI agents to analyze that data, turning months of manual analysis into hours.

We’re sharing how this program has further scaled up from supporting individual scientists to developing a large number of scientific partnerships with institutions and foundations to support researchers across many scientific fields. Many of these projects will also produce public goods that benefit the wider scientific community: open datasets, open-source software, open standards, and shared libraries. We look forward to seeing how AI resources can expand what scientists can attempt and lead to new discoveries.

Science funders and societies play an enormous role in finding and funding original, high-impact projects. We’re sharing Claude credits with the following organizations, which will distribute these resources to ambitious researchers aiming to use AI for scientific research:

Leading research institutions produce some of the world’s most important scientific advances, data, instruments, and tools. These institutional partners will use Claude credits inside their organizations to enable scientific discovery:

As part of this work, we’re also continuing to support innovative research by providing Claude credits directly to specific research initiatives, focusing on problems with the potential for large public impact. The new projects are:

Many of these collaborations are still in their early stages, and we’re eager to see how they can support novel research and scientific discovery. We look forward to sharing the impact of this work and showcasing new ways of working in these scientific fields.

As AI changes how science is done, our AI for Science program will continue to support and collaborate with scientists, institutions, and foundations. We hope to expand these efforts to even more partners around the world.
cim: Az Anthropic 20 tudományos partnerrel bővíti AI for Science programját
lead: Az Anthropic ingyenes Claude-kreditekkel és együttműködésekkel támogatja a tudományos kutatásokat végző szervezeteket.
osszefoglalo:
Az Anthropic bejelentette, hogy az [AI for Science](https://www.anthropic.com/news/ai-for-science-program) programjának bővítésével 20 tudományos alapítvánnyal, intézménnyel és kutatócsoporttal lép partnerségre világszerte. A kezdeményezés célja, hogy ingyenes Claude-kreditek biztosításával gyorsítsa fel a nagy hatású tudományos projekteket a biológia, az orvostudomány, a fizika és a klímakutatás területén.

A partnerek között szerepel a HHMI Janelia Research Campus, amellyel közösen a laboratóriumi eszközök biztonságos AI-vezérlését szolgáló Model Hardware Standardot fejlesztik, valamint az Allen Institute, amely AI-ügynökökkel gyorsítja fel a komplex agy- és sejtkutatási adatok elemzését.

A támogatott projektek jelentős része nyílt adatbázisokat, nyílt forráskódú szoftvereket és közös szabványokat hoz majd létre, amelyeket a teljes tudományos közösség szabadon használhat.
miert_szamit: A kutatás-fejlesztésben dolgozó szakemberek és elemzők számára a kezdeményezés megmutatja, hogyan automatizálhatók az **összetett adatfeldolgozási folyamatok** AI-ügynökök segítségével.
